7f3a.question: Was the van's rear door open when it backed up?
7f3a.answer: Yes. The rear doors are open from 21:11:19 onward - visible as the van turns. Two figures approach from the right at 21:11:41.
7f3a.reasoning: Re-decoded 45 s at native resolution, 4 fps (181 frames). Frames up to 21:11:18 show the van at an angle with the rear face occluded by the door pillar, which is why the 1 fps live caption could not commit either way. At 21:11:19 the van yaws roughly 15 degrees and both rear doors are visible, swung outward past the body line; the left door edge casts a shadow onto the loading apron that tracks with the door, not the body, confirming it is open rather than a reflection. The doors remain open in every subsequent frame. At 21:11:41 two figures enter from the right edge and reach the rear of the van by 21:11:47. No cargo movement is visible within the analysed range.

b2c9.question: Is a vehicle stopped in front of the fire door?
b2c9.answer: Confirmed. A white panel van is stationary across the marked fire door bay for the full 45 s window.
b2c9.reasoning: Native-resolution re-read shows the painted fire-door keep-clear hatching fully occluded by the vehicle body from 21:11:11 to the end of the range. The van does not translate between frames; only the rear doors move.

d41e.question: Is a vehicle stopped in front of the fire door?
d41e.answer: No vehicle. The dark region in front of the fire door is a shadow cast by headlight glare crossing the roller door.
d41e.reasoning: At native resolution the region has no edges consistent with a vehicle body, no wheels and no parallax against the door frame across 60 frames. The apparent shape tracks a moving light source off-frame to the left. The 1 fps live caption resolved it as a halted object; at 4 fps it is clearly a travelling reflection.
